$comment: The model pipeline's manifest. Every asset Onward ships is listed here with the licence it
arrives under and the URL it came from, so the SaaS licence question is answerable later
without redoing #4's research.
SCALE. 'target' is the real-world size the asset should read at, in metres, on the named axis.
The model matrix maps one unit to one metre (src/map/model-matrix.ts), so scale is solved as
target.metres / the measured extent on that axis. Source units are worthless across kits: a
suburban house is 0.74 units tall while a van is 2.75 units long.
The axis is HEIGHT for every Kenney model, and that is the finding that matters here. Kenney's
vehicles are modelled faithfully in cross-section and heavily compressed in length — a
double-deck carriage is 1.28 wide, 1.92 tall and only 2.5 long, where a real one is 26 m long
on a 3 m body. Solving for a true 26 m length gives a carriage 20 m TALL, which towers over an
8 m guesthouse and destroys the one-world read. Solving for a true height instead leaves each
piece stubby — which is the toy register the Diorama already committed to — and the set sits
together. The trains ship as a/b/c segments precisely so length comes from coupling them.
The converted airliner is the opposite case: faithful in plan, exaggerated in fin height, so it
is solved on wingspan.
The Stay Marker is solved on height for a different reason, and #21 is where it matters. It is
not a portrait of anyone's hotel — it is the single building that says a bed is booked here — so
it is chosen to be SPOTTED. Reading it on its 40 m height rather than a footprint is what buys
that: the pixel law in src/map/model-scale.ts takes an asset's longest axis, so a tall building
crosses the drawing threshold at a lower zoom than a wide one of the same volume. The corollary
caught #21 out and is worth stating: a SLENDER tower is worse, not better, because at the
threshold it is 15 px tall and only 15/slenderness wide.
ORIENTATION. 'forward' is the direction the model's nose points in its own source axes, and it is
DECLARED rather than inferred. Inference was tried first and is not trustworthy: the largest
horizontal extent is the airliner's WINGSPAN, not its fuselage, and an outer-fifth taper test
reads a van's cargo box as its nose.
Each declaration has a witness. Seven of the nine vehicles are confirmed by Kenney's own node
names — `wheel-front-right` at z +0.76 against `wheel-back-right` at -0.76 — which is the author
stating it outright. The two single-node watercraft have no such names and were settled by the
station profiles in scripts/models/stations.mjs plus docs/models/contact-sheet.png. build.mjs
re-runs the best available witness on every build and warns when it disagrees with the
declaration, so a newly added asset gets flagged rather than silently trusted.
Every model in the set turned out to face +Z, Kenney's own convention and the one the converted
airliner was matched to.
Fingerprinted Kenney URLs go stale when a pack is updated. If one 404s, re-read the pack page
linked as 'page' and replace both 'url' and 'bytes'.

assets.note: A small open longtail-ish boat: the island-hop register. Reads at ~4.9 m long.
Funnelled passenger liner, near fore-aft symmetric. The bow is the finer end: tip half-beam 0.30 units against 0.94 at the stern. Reads at ~17 m long.
Double-deck set, nose — the cab end is both lower and narrower. The sleeper read; #4 judged the kit's own carriages freight-bodied.
Middle segment, fore-aft symmetric: yaw is arbitrary and set to 0 for consistency.
High-speed set, nose — tapers from 0.65 to 0.24 half-beam at the +z tip. The daytime intercity read.
No CC0 bus exists anywhere #4 checked, and a van is the truer depiction of a minibus hop regardless. The bonnet is the +z end: body height falls from 1.35 to 0.72 units. Reads at ~5.3 m long.

The one building that means a bed is booked here — a 40 m hotel tower, 398 tris. It does NOT depict the accommodation: #21 ruled that every non-Shortlisted Stay stands the same building whether the real thing is a Sukhumvit condo or a beach hut, because the building's job is to be *spotted*, not to be accurate. Highrise for exactly that reason: read on its 40 m height it crosses #20's 15 px at z14.8 against the old guesthouse's z17, so a booking announces itself two zoom levels earlier with STAY_MIN_PX untouched. Scaled by height like every Kenney asset: 40 m to the parapet on a ~17.6 × 20.0 m footprint. Picked over towers b/c/d on slenderness — the pixel law reads the LONGEST axis, which for a tower is its height, so a slender tower arrives 15 px tall and only 4 px wide; tower-a's h/foot of 2.0 stays a block rather than a stick, and its window grid and entrance canopy read as a hotel.

Untextured, which is an advantage: Onward owns its colour. Solved on wingspan — the fuselage is the SHORTER horizontal axis on this model, and its fin is proportionally tall, so neither length nor height is a safe reference. Reads at 60 m span, ~46.5 m long.

notTaken: building-sample-tower-b/c/d as the Stay Marker — all three are CC0 and already in this kit, and #21 measured them side by side. The pixel law reads an asset's LONGEST axis, and for a tower that is its height, so at the 15 px threshold a tower is 15 px tall and h/foot px wide: tower-d (h/foot 3.42) arrives as a 4 px stick and tower-c (2.46) a 6 px one. tower-b (1.51) is chunkiest but at 40 m its footprint is 23 × 27 m, which reads as a block rather than a tower. tower-a (2.00) is the balance. Not shipped, because #17 already left three unreachable train GLBs in the bundle and once was enough

building-sample-house-a/b/c as the Stay Marker — house-b was the incumbent and is what #21 replaced. Kenney's pre-assembled houses are cream pitched-gable European suburbia: wrong for a Bangkok condo, wrong for a Thai beach bungalow, and only ever right for the guesthouse it happened to resemble
Kenney Retro Urban Kit — 22 discrete textures, breaks the one-atlas-per-kit convention
Kenney City Kit Suburban — North-American suburbia, wrong register for a Stay
Kenney Pirate Kit as a Stay — its structures are docks, not huts. Bookmarked for island dressing
Quaternius Small Ship via Poly Pizza — 5,578 tris, twice the densest Kenney model
Poly Pizza CC-BY airliner — would add a permanent attribution surface Onward does not otherwise need
Poly Pizza Hut (CC0, 632 tris) — deferred to #11, where there is a palette to judge it against
Any Poly Pizza model by an unknown uploader — the site has no reachable terms page, so a label is a claim
The model titled Boeing 747 — CC0 waives copyright, never trademark
